evals.prompt: Define ideation in 2-3 sentences. Name its two halves and the core claim that organizes the practice.
expected_elements: Defines it as producing many concept variants then converging on a worthwhile subset
Names the two halves: a divergent (generation) mode and a convergent (selection) mode
States the core claim that quantity precedes quality / generation and judgment must be separated
Operates on a well-framed problem

evals.prompt: Why must generation (divergent) and judgment (convergent) be kept as strictly separate modes rather than allowed to run together?
expected_elements: Judging an idea costs cognitive effort and judgment running in parallel with generation suppresses generation
Teams that judge as they ideate produce fewer ideas
Mixed-mode ideas skew toward the safe middle of the distribution
Splitting the modes widens the divergent field so convergent pruning is meaningful

evals.prompt: What is the role of forced quantity and a worst-possible-idea round, and what do they trade off against?
expected_elements: The first ~three ideas are the obvious ones any competitor has also had
Interesting ideas live in the second half of a forced-quantity round, past the obvious
Worst-possible-idea disinhibits and exposes which norms were holding the design back
The trade is polish/comfort for range — quantity is prioritized over early refinement

evals.prompt: Name concrete divergent techniques and convergent techniques an agent could run, and what each is for.
expected_elements: Divergent: Crazy 8s, brainwriting, SCAMPER, worst-possible-idea, headlines-from-the-future, analogous inspiration
Convergent: dot voting, NUF test (New/Useful/Feasible), impact/effort 2x2, weighted decision matrices, assumption-testing prioritization
Divergent techniques flood the field; convergent techniques prune against criteria
Brainwriting bypasses dominant voices; Crazy 8s time-boxes eight sketches in eight minutes

evals.prompt: A team is about to run a convergent selection round. What must happen with the selection criteria, and when?
expected_elements: Selection criteria must be named in writing BEFORE voting begins
Criteria-first makes the choice defensible rather than political
Criteria must not be retrofitted to justify the popular choice
Convergent methods (dot voting, NUF, weighted matrix) apply the explicit criteria

evals.prompt: A teammate asks the ideation skill to model the bounded contexts and domain events for the order-fulfillment system. Is that in scope? Why or why not?
expected_elements: Not in scope — that is event-storming (collaborative engineering domain discovery)
Ideation generates a variety of solution concepts, it does not model domain events/aggregates
Correctly distinguishes generating concept variety from seeking one correct domain model
Redirects to event-storming (or conceptual-modeling for a single correct model)

evals.prompt: A stakeholder says 'ideation is just brainstorming — throw out ideas until something sticks.' Correct the mental model.
expected_elements: An undisciplined free-for-all that judges as it generates produces fewer and safer ideas
The value comes from strictly separating generation from judgment
Forced quantity is needed to get past the obvious first ideas
The discipline (silent time-boxed divergent rounds, then criteria-first convergent selection) is what widens then sharpens the field

evals.prompt: What would you check to verify an ideation session was run well?
expected_elements: A divergent round produced a large set (e.g. 20+ variants, or 8 per participant in Crazy 8s) before any convergence
Selection criteria were written before voting, not retrofitted
Selected concepts are materially different from each other, not variations on one idea
At least one selected concept is uncomfortable/unfamiliar; time-boxes were enforced and modes did not re-merge
